newsitem.title: USA: Idaho rivers overflow, 7 counties declare disasters.
newsitem.headline: Idaho rivers overflow, 7 counties declare disasters.

text.p: The winter's near record snowpack has been melting into floodwaters, prompting seven Idaho counties to declare disasters as other counties braced for overflowing rivers, state officials said Saturday.
"The heavy snowpack is melting and running into the reservoirs and the rivers," state Disaster Services spokesman Jim Ball said. "The result is heavy flooding."

The counties where flood disasters have been declared included Custer, Madison, Jefferson, Bonneville, Bingham and Twin Falls, Ball said. In the coming days, several other counties could be hard hit, he warned.
Major roadways in central and southeastern Idaho were flooded, including Interstate 15, a north-south roadway linking Blackfoot to Idaho Falls.
As many as 60 homes and farms just outside Blackfoot, in Idaho's potato growing Bingham County, were flooded.
"It's coming in slowly," said Rick Just, a spokesman for the Bingham County emergency center. "The water is relentless."
Fifteen homes south of the city of Firth have been flooded and more flooding was expected in the area. A school was being used as a staging point for sandbagging efforts.
In Rigby, the Red Cross set up an emergency shelter for flood victims at the local high school. Sheriff's deputies were standing by to evacuate the elderly and disabled.
Hundreds of people in and around Roberts, along the swollen Snake River, were evacuated.
Portions of Roberts were under five feet of water. At least 35 homes in the town and in surrounding areas were damaged, said Dick Larsen, a spokesman for the Jefferson County sheriff's department.
Larsen said, however, that the worst appeared to be over. "Unless something catastrophic happens, this is probably about as bad as it's going to get."
